abstract: Inspects and maintains sea-state operational certifications and passenger throughput logs
system_message:
You are Maritime safety inspector (MSO). The Maritime safety inspector (MSO) is responsible for inspecting and maintaining sea-state operational certifications and passenger throughput logs, as well as recording drydock hull integrity testing results for candidate vessels.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Inspects and maintains sea-state operational certifications and passenger throughput logs（SEACERT）
information_points.content:
MSO-SEACERT-5HS：For Atlantic Marine Transit Consortium, the American Bureau of Shipping inspection register confirms that sea-state operation certification verified for the flagship evacuation vessel is true for operations in Beaufort force 7 and sea-state 5, and the rapid evacuation drill record confirms a certified passenger boarding throughput of 600 passengers/h across its dual-ramp gangway configuration.
MSO-SEACERT-8VX：For Cape Fear Heavy Marine Transport, the American Bureau of Shipping inspection register confirms that sea-state operation certification verified for the flagship evacuation vessel is true for operations in Beaufort force 7 and sea-state 5, and the rapid evacuation drill record demonstrates a certified passenger boarding throughput of 450 passengers/h across its dual-ramp gangway configuration.
MSO-SEACERT-JQO：For Outer Banks Catamaran Fleet, the American Bureau of Shipping inspection register confirms that sea-state operation certification verified for the flagship evacuation vessel is true for operations in Beaufort force 7 and sea-state 5, while the rapid evacuation drill record documents a certified passenger boarding throughput of 380 passengers/h across its dual-ramp gangway configuration.

information_points.title: Drydock hull integrity testing（HULLINSP）
information_points.content:
MSO-HULLINSP-RMA：For Atlantic Marine Transit Consortium, the non-destructive testing registry records an ultrasonic hull plate thickness score of 82 points on a 100-point scale for the primary passenger hull plating.
MSO-HULLINSP-CLQ：For Cape Fear Heavy Marine Transport, the non-destructive testing registry records an ultrasonic hull plate thickness score of 94 points on a 100-point scale for the primary passenger hull plating.
MSO-HULLINSP-ZRE：For Outer Banks Catamaran Fleet, the non-destructive testing registry records an ultrasonic hull plate thickness score of 88 points on a 100-point scale for the primary passenger hull plating.
